metadata.title: 1967 Case 51
metadata.original_presentation: A fifty-two-year-old woman entered the hospital because of melena. One year previously, after an episode of vomiting, a gastrointestinal series showed esophageal varices.

required.content: What is the patient's history of gastrointestinal bleeding?
required.response: The patient had several episodes of melena over the past year, each lasting a few days.

teaching_points.content: Recurrent melena can indicate ongoing gastrointestinal bleeding, often associated with varices or ulcers.

required.content: What is the patient's history of alcohol consumption?
required.response: Throughout her adult life, she consumed up to a bottle of wine daily.

teaching_points.content: Chronic alcohol consumption is a risk factor for liver cirrhosis and esophageal varices.

required.content: What is the patient's past medical history?
required.response: The patient had a history of jaundice 20 years ago, diabetes diagnosed a year ago, and a bilateral sympathectomy for high blood pressure.

teaching_points.content: Past medical history can provide clues to current health issues, such as the link between jaundice and liver disease.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Esophageal varices due to portal hypertension
additional_information_needed: Abdominal ultrasound to assess liver and portal vein
Endoscopy to evaluate current status of varices

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Peptic ulcer disease
supporting_evidence: Alcohol consumption which can contribute to ulcer formation

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Gastric cancer
refuting_evidence: No weight loss or other systemic symptoms reported

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Liver cirrhosis
additional_information_needed: Assessment for signs of liver failure

required.content: What were the findings on the physical examination?
required.response: The patient was pale, sallow, and lethargic with erythematous palms, clubbing of the digits, and a firm liver edge palpable 5 fingerbreadths below the right costal margin.

teaching_points.content: Physical signs such as clubbing and hepatomegaly can indicate chronic liver disease.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Cirrhosis with portal hypertension
supporting_evidence: Esophageal varices noted a year ago
Firm liver edge palpable 5 fingerbreadths below the right costal margin

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Gastrointestinal bleeding secondary to esophageal varices
supporting_evidence: Several episodes of melena over the past year
Esophageal varices noted a year ago
additional_information_needed: Endoscopy to confirm source of bleeding

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Alcoholic liver disease
supporting_evidence: History of consuming up to a bottle of wine daily

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH)
supporting_evidence: Diagnosis of diabetes a year ago

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Peptic ulcer disease
refuting_evidence: History of alcohol use and liver disease

required.content: What were the key laboratory findings?
required.response: The hematocrit was 30%, white-cell count 4900, platelets decreased, bilirubin 1.4 mg, and ammonia 150 μg.

teaching_points.content: Laboratory tests can help assess liver function and the severity of liver disease.

required.content: What imaging studies were performed and what did they show?
required.response: X-ray films of the chest showed slight prominence of the left ventricle and pulmonary vasculature; a gastrointestinal series revealed esophageal and gastric varices.

teaching_points.content: Imaging can confirm the presence of varices and assess cardiac and pulmonary status.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Cirrhosis with portal hypertension
supporting_evidence: History of alcohol consumption up to a bottle of wine daily
Esophageal varices noted on gastrointestinal series
Firm liver edge palpable 5 fingerbreadths below the right costal margin
additional_information_needed: Liver function tests (AST, ALT, ALP, GGT)

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Alcoholic liver disease
supporting_evidence: History of alcohol consumption up to a bottle of wine daily
Firm liver edge palpable 5 fingerbreadths below the right costal margin
additional_information_needed: Liver function tests (AST, ALT, ALP, GGT)

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH)
supporting_evidence: History of diabetes diagnosed a year ago
additional_information_needed: Liver function tests (AST, ALT, ALP, GGT)

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Gastrointestinal bleeding secondary to varices
supporting_evidence: Several episodes of melena over the past year
Esophageal and gastric varices on gastrointestinal series
additional_information_needed: Endoscopy to assess the extent of varices and potential bleeding sites

required.content: What treatments were administered during the hospital stay?
required.response: Magnesium citrate and neomycin were administered, and a side-to-side portacaval shunt was performed.

teaching_points.content: Management of variceal bleeding may include medications and surgical interventions like shunt procedures.

final_diagnosis.name: Posthepatitic cirrhosis
supporting_evidence: History of alcohol use and jaundice
